summary: Which kinds of blood is it forbidden to eat, with the punishment of kares? This mishnah lists the blood one is liable for and the blood one is not.

chunks.en: Blood from shechting a farm animal,
chunks.st: If one consumed an olive-bulk of blood that spurted during the slaughter of a domesticated animal,

chunks.en: a wild animal, or birds,
chunks.st: an undomesticated animal, or a bird,

chunks.en: whether non-kosher or kosher,
chunks.st: whether it is a kosher or non-kosher species;

chunks.en: blood from stabbing,
chunks.st: or if one consumed blood that flowed after stabbing an animal or killing it in a manner other than by ritual slaughter,

chunks.en: blood from tearing,
chunks.st: or blood that spurted after ripping the animal’s windpipe or gullet,

chunks.en: and blood from letting blood that the animal's life goes out with,
chunks.st: or blood that spurted during bloodletting with which the soul departs,

chunks.en: one is liable for it.
chunks.st: one is liable to receive karet for consuming it intentionally or to bring a sin offering for consuming it unwittingly.

chunks.en: Blood of the spleen,
chunks.st: But with regard to blood of the spleen,

chunks.en: blood of the heart,
chunks.st: blood of the heart,

chunks.en: blood of eggs,
chunks.st: blood of eggs,

chunks.en: blood of fish, blood of grasshoppers,
chunks.st: blood of grasshoppers,

chunks.en: blood that oozes out at the end,
chunks.st: or blood of exudate [tamtzit], i.e., that oozes from the neck of the animal after the initial spurt of its slaughter concludes,

chunks.en: one is not liable for them.
chunks.st: one is not liable for consuming it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says one is liable for blood that oozes out.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems one liable in the case of blood of exudate.

summary: Does a person who is not sure he did me'ilah bring an asham taluy? Rabbi Akiva says yes, and the Sages say no. Rabbi Tarfon suggests a way to pay and bring one asham that works either way.
stIntro: This mishna resumes discussion of the provisional guilt offering addressed in the previous chapter.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says one must bring
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva deems one liable to bring a provisional guilt offering for

chunks.en: an asham taluy for a doubt of me'ilah,
chunks.st: a case where he is uncertain whether he is guilty of misuse of consecrated property,
chunks.stMore: a transgression that renders one liable to bring a definite guilt offering (see Leviticus 5:15).

words.note: Using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for oneself.

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is free.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis deem him exempt,
chunks.stMore: as one brings a provisional guilt offering only in a case of uncertainty as to whether he is liable to bring a sin offering, not a guilt offering.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Akiva agrees
chunks.st: And Rabbi Akiva concedes

chunks.en: that he does not pay for his me'ilah
chunks.st: that one does not bring payment for his misuse

chunks.en: until he knows for sure,
chunks.st: until it becomes definitely known to him that he is guilty of misuse,

chunks.en: and then he brings a sure asham with it.
chunks.st: as then he will bring a definite guilt offering with his payment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon said:

chunks.en: "Why should this person bring two ashamos?
chunks.st: For what purpose does that person bring two guilt offerings, one provisional and one definite?

chunks.en: Rather, he should pay for the me'ilah and an extra fifth,
chunks.st: Rather, at the outset one brings the payment for misuse of consecrated property and its additional payment of one-fifth,
chunks.stMore: as mandated by Torah law,

chunks.en: and bring an asham worth two sela'im,
chunks.st: and he will then bring a guilt offering worth two sela

words.note: A sela is a silver coin.

chunks.en: and say: If I surely did me'ilah,
chunks.st: and say: If it is certain that I misused consecrated property,

chunks.en: this is for my me'ilah and this is my asham.
chunks.st: this is payment for my misuse and this is my definite guilt offering.

chunks.en: And if it is a doubt,
chunks.st: And if it is uncertain whether I misused consecrated property,

chunks.en: the money is a gift, and the asham is an asham taluy.
chunks.st: the money is a contribution to the Temple fund for the purchase of communal offerings and the guilt offering is provisional,

chunks.en: For the same kind of korban that he brings when he knows,
chunks.st: as from the same type of animal that one brings a guilt offering for a case where it is known to him that he is guilty of misuse,

chunks.en: he brings when he does not know."
chunks.st: he likewise brings a guilt offering for a case where it is unknown to him.

summary: Rabbi Akiva answers Rabbi Tarfon that his idea is good only for a small me'ilah. The mishnah also teaches about a woman whose bird chatas was brought because of a doubt.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says: The statement of

chunks.en: "Your words make sense for a small me'ilah.
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon appears correct in the case of minimal misuse,

chunks.en: But if he has
chunks.st: but in a case where he is confronted with

chunks.en: a doubtful me'ilah worth a hundred maneh,
chunks.st: a case of uncertainty with regard to misuse valued at ten thousand dinars,

words.note: A maneh is a hundred dinars.

chunks.en: isn't it better for him to bring an asham
chunks.st: would it not be preferable for him that he will now bring a provisional guilt offering

chunks.en: worth two sela'im, and not pay for a doubtful
chunks.st: valued at two sela and he will not bring payment now for uncertain

chunks.en: me'ilah worth a hundred maneh?"
chunks.st: misuse valued at ten thousand dinars?

chunks.en: So Rabbi Akiva agrees
chunks.st: The mishna concludes: Apparently, Rabbi Akiva concedes

chunks.en: with Rabbi Tarfon about a small me'ilah.
chunks.st: to Rabbi Tarfon in the case of minimal misuse.
chunks.stMore: He agrees that at the outset one brings payment for misuse and its additional payment of one-fifth, and conditionally brings a guilt offering.

chunks.en: A woman who brought a bird chatas because of a doubt:
chunks.st: Apropos the previous case in which one brings the same type of animal when liability is certain as when liability is uncertain, this mishna teaches: With regard to a woman who brought a bird sin offering in a case of uncertainty
chunks.stMore: whether she miscarried a fetus that would have rendered her liable to bring a sin offering or whether what she expelled would not render her liable to bring an offering, in which case this sin offering may not be eaten by priests,

chunks.en: if, before its neck was pinched,
chunks.st: the halakha is as follows: If before the nape of the neck of the bird was pinched

words.note: Melikah: the Kohen pinches the bird's neck with his fingernail.

chunks.en: she found out that she surely had a baby,
chunks.st: it became known to her that she certainly gave birth,
chunks.stMore: i.e., miscarried, in a manner that obligates her to bring a sin offering,

chunks.en: she should make it a sure chatas.
chunks.st: she should render the offering a definite sin offering,

chunks.he: שֶׁמִּמִּין שֶׁהִיא מְבִיאָה עַל לֹא הוֹדַע,
chunks.en: For the same kind of korban she brings when she does not know,
chunks.st: as from the same type of animal that she brings a sin offering for a case where it is known to her that she miscarried,

chunks.en: she brings when she knows.
chunks.st: she brings a sin offering for a case where it is unknown to her.

summary: A person ate one of two pieces of meat, one regular and one holy, and he does not know which. Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yosei argue about what korban he brings.
stIntro: The mishna resumes discussion of the provisional guilt offering.

chunks.he: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל חֻלִּין וַחֲתִיכָה שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ,
chunks.en: A piece of regular meat and a piece of holy meat:
chunks.st: If one had a piece of non-sacred meat and a piece of sacrificial meat,

chunks.en: he is free. Rabbi Akiva says he must bring an asham taluy.
chunks.st: he is exempt from the obligation to bring a guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property. Rabbi Akiva deems him liable to bring a provisional guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with his opinion in the previous mishna that one brings a provisional guilt offering even in a case of uncertainty with regard to misuse.

chunks.en: If he then ate the second one,
chunks.st: If he then ate the second piece,

chunks.en: he brings a sure asham.
chunks.st: he brings a definite guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: as it is certain that he ate the sacrificial meat.

chunks.en: If one person ate the first one,
chunks.st: If one person ate the first piece

chunks.en: and another came and ate the second one,
chunks.st: and another person came and ate the second piece,

chunks.en: this one brings an asham taluy,
chunks.st: this first person brings a provisional guilt offering

chunks.en: and that one brings an asham taluy.
chunks.st: and that second person brings a provisional guilt offering;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: both of them bring one asham together.
chunks.st: Both of them bring one definite guilt offering as partners,
chunks.stMore: and they stipulate that the one who ate the non-sacred meat grants his share of the animal to the one who ate the sacrificial meat, and the guilt offering is sacrificed on his behalf.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: two people do not bring one asham.
chunks.st: Two people do not bring one guilt offering, as one may not sacrifice atonement offerings conditionally.
